Last night, she built an entire app, without writing a single line of code herself.
She described what she wanted, and an AI wrote it for her.
This is vibe coding. And millions of people are doing it, every single day.
Apps that took a team months now take one person an afternoon.
But there's a catch. Nobody is keeping track of what the AI actually built.
Somewhere in Maya's code, there's a secret key, pasted in plain text, for anyone to find.
The AI also added a package that doesn't exist. Or one that's a single letter off a popular one. Exactly the kind of name an attacker loves to register.
In the files that tell the AI what to do, there are characters no human can see. But the AI reads them, and follows them.
And when the next change breaks everything, there's no record of the last version that worked. The context, the screenshots, the reasons why, all lost somewhere in a chat history.
Vibe code is shipping without a safety net.
So we built one. Depotex gives every vibe-coded project a safe home.
Each time the AI finishes a change, it checks in: the code, its memory, the known gaps, and screenshots of what it built.
Every push is checked on the way in. Secrets and hidden characters are refused at the door.
Made-up and look-alike packages are flagged, before anyone installs them.
And when a change breaks the tests, Depotex knows the last check-in that passed, so the AI can go straight back to it.
AI tools push and pull projects directly. And people can find any project, by name, by date, or by what it looks like.
So keep vibing. Just don't lose the plot.
